item.title: In Canada and at Home, Deference to Trump Turns to Defiance on Tariffs and Other Issues

Kennedy, John F, Center for the Performing Arts
item.media:description: World leaders and domestic institutions are showing less willingness to submit to President Trump’s will.

item.title: At Trump’s IndyCar Race, a V.I.P. Invitation Became a Diplomatic Snub
item.description: Foreign ambassadors were promised free food and drinks, misting fans and shaded seats during the event. Then some of them were uninvited.
item.dc:creator: Anton Troianovski and Eric Schmitt
item.media:credit: Anna Rose Layden for The New York Times
item.media:description: White House staff members watch the Freedom 250 Grand Prix on the National Mall last week. Some ambassadors were uninvited.

item.title: Dolly Parton, Country Music Superstar Whose Songs Spoke to Millions, Dies at 80
item.description: Known for her outsize persona, appearance and talent, she rose from rural poverty to become a top-selling singer, songwriter and entrepreneur.
item.dc:creator: Bill Friskics-Warren
item.media:description: Dolly Parton in 1975. She was likened to the Big Rock Candy Mountain, the Depression-era symbol of abundance. Her music confronted privation and loss even as it radiated possibility and hope.

item.title: Dolly Parton Had the Voice, and Concerns, of an Earth Angel
item.description: Parton gave hopeful expression to songs she wrote about the hard times and hard-won triumphs of her life.
item.dc:creator: Lindsay Zoladz
item.media:description: Some of Parton’s most celebrated songs recounted scenes from her life, told with cinematic detail.

item.title: Dolly Parton Died After Brief Battle With Cancer
item.description: Parton had recently canceled a Las Vegas residency because of health issues. A spokesman said she was admitted to a cancer center in Nashville on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Julia Jacobs
item.media:description: In the past, Dolly Parton said she had dealt with challenges involving her immune and digestive systems.

item.title: Dolly Parton’s Death Hits Home for Tennesseans: ‘She Was One of Us’
item.description: The country music star kept her home state at the forefront of her music and work. “She inspired Tennesseans to be better,” one resident said.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane
item.media:credit: Landon Edwards for The New York Times
item.media:description: As the nation mourned Dolly Parton’s death on Tuesday, the grief was perhaps the most profound in Tennessee.

item.title: Graham, and Trump, Triumph: Six Takeaways From South Carolina’s Senate Runoff
item.description: President Trump went all in for Senator Darline Graham in a primary runoff on Tuesday. It worked, preserving his undefeated streak in Republican Senate primaries this year.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Sean Rayford for The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham’s victory on Tuesday showed President Trump’s continued ability to move Republican primary voters, especially when he goes all in on a race.

item.title: Mike Mazzei, Backed by Trump, Wins Oklahoma Primary for Governor
item.description: Mike Mazzei, a former state senator who lent more than $11 million of his own money to his campaign, narrowly defeated the state’s attorney general, Gentner Drummond.
item.dc:creator: J. David Goodman
item.media:credit: Jake Ramsey/Oklahoma Watch, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Mike Mazzei delivering his closing remarks at a televised debate this month in the Oklahoma Republican governor’s race.

item.title: Everton Blair Jr. Wins Race to Fill David Scott’s House Seat in Georgia
item.description: Everton Blair Jr. will serve until January in the seat long held by Mr. Scott, who died in April. Mr. Blair is not competing in the general election for the next full term in the deep-blue district.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:credit: Arvin Temkar/Atlanta Journal-Constitution, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Everton Blair Jr. will head to Washington for the remaining months of Representative David Scott’s term.

item.title: Canada Fires Back in Trade War Against Trump With Up to 50% Tariffs
item.description: Canada said the higher levies, on items from aluminum foil to dishwashers to fish, would help protect workers, producers and manufacturers harmed by new Trump tariffs.

item.title: Trump’s Canada Tariffs Rely on Untested Law

item.title: A Surrogate Fled to Texas to Avoid an Abortion. Now She Wants Custody of the Baby.
